chunks: And among what Ayyūb ibn al-Ḥurr narrated from ʿUbayd ibn Zurārah, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man afflicted by flowing blood. He said: He performs wudu (ablution) and repeats. He said: And if it is not flowing, he performs wudu (ablution) and continues from where he left off. He said: And he does that between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah.

key_terms.بَيْنَ الصَّفَا وَالْمَرْوَةِ: during the saʿy between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah
key_terms.وَبَنَى: he continues from where he left off

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if flowing or non-flowing blood occurs during worship or saʿy between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding bleeding during an act of worship. If the blood is flowing, the person performs wudu (ablution) and repeats, whereas if it is not flowing, he performs wudu (ablution) and continues; the same ruling applies during the saʿy between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah.
